_comment: Which Wikipedia language is “home” for which country.
Articles are ALWAYS fetched in English plus the language of the country the
point lies in – that's the whole point of this file. The key is `country`
already decides the Drive folder and a second lookup of the same would drift
A POINT'S COUNTRY COMES FROM THE REGION, NOT THE POINT. A region extract is
clipped at the region border (osm.fr cuts it by relation), so a point in it
lies in the region's country. Reverse-geocoding borders would be a whole
pipeline for a few border points – and those are caught anyway: a language
the object NAMES ITSELF in a tag (`wikipedia=pl:Rysy`) is fetched too. A point
on the Polish side of a ridge gets the Polish article without anyone knowing
Several languages in a list are for countries with several official
languages; all are fetched. A country missing here gets English and what its
objects name themselves – and the run says so aloud, so it can be added.
